questions.question_text:
A florist is paid $\$26.80$ per hour and works $7$ hours a day for $4$ days.
Find her total pay.

options.why: Found the pay for one day only, forgetting to multiply by the $4$ days worked.
Multiplied the rate by the $4$ days instead of by the $28$ hours worked.
Multiplied by the $4$ days a second time after already using $7 \times 4 = 28$ hours.

questions.question_text:
A café worker earned $\$715.50$ for $27$ hours of work.
Find her hourly rate of pay.

options.why: Divided by $54$ hours, wrongly treating the amount as a fortnight's pay.
Subtracted the number of hours from the pay instead of dividing by it.
Made a place-value slip in the division, giving a rate ten times too small.

questions.question_text:
A mechanic is paid $\$29.40$ per hour for the first $38$ hours each week, and time and a half for any hours beyond that.
Find his total pay for a week in which he works $44$ hours.

options.why: Paid all $44$ hours at the normal rate, ignoring the penalty rate on the extra hours.
Applied time and a half to all $44$ hours instead of only the $6$ overtime hours.
Used double time instead of time and a half for the $6$ overtime hours.

questions.question_text:
A supermarket department manager is paid a salary of $\$85\,800$ p.a.
How much is this per month?

options.why: Divided by $52$ weeks, giving the weekly pay rather than the monthly pay.
Divided by $26$ fortnights, giving the fortnightly pay rather than the monthly pay.
Multiplied the weekly pay by $4$, treating a month as exactly four weeks.

questions.question_text:
A worker in a shoe factory is paid $\$2.45$ for each pair of laces she threads.
Find the smallest number of pairs she must thread to earn at least $\$300$.

options.why: Rounded $122.4\ldots$ down, which leaves the earnings short of $\$300$.
Divided by a rounded rate of $\$2.50$ instead of the actual $\$2.45$.
Multiplied the target by the rate instead of dividing by it.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\$300}{\$2.45}$
$=122.44\ldots$
Part of a pair cannot be threaded, so she must thread $123$ pairs.

questions.question_text:
A furniture sales assistant is paid a retainer of $\$420$ per week plus a commission of $2.5\%$ of sales.
Find her total pay in a week in which her sales are $\$18\,600$.

options.why: Gave the commission alone, leaving out the $\$420$ retainer.
Added the retainer to the sales before taking $2.5\%$, instead of adding it afterwards.
Used $0.25$ instead of $0.025$ when converting $2.5\%$ to a decimal.

questions.question_text:
A carpet salesperson is paid $3\%$ commission on the first $\$20\,000$ of sales and $5\%$ on any sales above $\$20\,000$.
Find the commission earned on sales of $\$52\,000$.

options.why: Split the sales into the two bands correctly but swapped the rates, using $5\%$ on the first $\$20\,000$ and $3\%$ on the $\$32\,000$ above it.
Did not split the sales into bands and applied $5\%$ to the whole $\$52\,000$.
Did not split the sales into bands and applied $3\%$ to the whole $\$52\,000$, ignoring the higher rate on the top band.

questions.question_text:
A roof plumber is paid $\$36.20$ per hour and works $8$ hours a day for $5$ days.
He also receives a height allowance of $\$27$ for each day spent working on a roof, which was $3$ of the days.
Find his total pay for the week.

options.why: Left the height allowance out of the total pay altogether.
Paid the allowance for all $5$ days instead of only the $3$ roof days.
Added the allowance once rather than once for each of the $3$ roof days.

questions.question_text:
A hotel receptionist earns $\$1\,040$ per week.
She takes $4$ weeks of annual leave and is paid leave loading of $17.5\%$.
Find her total holiday pay.

options.why: Gave the leave loading by itself instead of the total holiday pay.
Gave four weeks of normal pay, leaving out the $17.5\%$ loading.
Added the loading to one week's pay instead of to four weeks' pay.

questions.question_text:
A pastry chef is paid $\$27.80$ per hour.
In one week she works $38$ ordinary hours, $5$ hours on Saturday at time and a half and $2$ hours on a public holiday at double time and a half.
She is also paid an early-start allowance of $\$21.50$ on each of $3$ mornings.
Find her total pay for the week, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Left the $\$21.50$ early-start allowance out of the total.
Paid all $45$ hours at the ordinary rate, ignoring both penalty rates.
Used double time instead of double time and a half for the public holiday hours.
